audits.title: Completed audit of the use of seclusion in the Approved Centre in Tallaght University Hospital following the introduction of an Integrated Care Pathway
audits.standard: Mental Health Commission rules governing the use of seclusion (13 rules)
audits.setting: Approved Centre (acute psychiatric unit), Tallaght University Hospital

cycle1.period: Before introduction of the Integrated Care Pathway (2012)
cycle1.result: Compliance across the 13 MHC rules ranged from 3% to 100%.

audits.intervention: Seclusion Integrated Care Pathway introduced in 2012 to record and monitor each seclusion episode.

cycle2.result: Compliance ranged from 69% to 100%; 100% compliance with five of the 13 rules.

audits.other_findings: Improvements in medical and nursing reviews, informing patients of reasons and likely duration of seclusion, and informing next of kin. An audit immediately after ICP introduction was also done.
audits.citation: Conlan-Trant R, Corrigan K, Whitty P. Completed audit of the use of seclusion in the Approved Centre in Tallaght University Hospital following the introduction of an Integrated Care Pathway. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S16-S16. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.100.

audits.title: Re-audit of use of seclusion in a tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit
audits.standard: Trust guidelines on seclusion monitoring and documentation, including consultant review within 24 hours and care plan modification
audits.setting: Tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit, London

cycle1.result: Average seclusion 30 h; assault on staff as indication in 50%; consultant review within 24 h documented in under 70%; care plan modified in 63%.

audits.intervention: Daily nursing safety huddles, weekly Incidence Reduction meetings and an ongoing QI project on restrictive practice.

cycle2.result: 18 patients, 46 incidents: average seclusion 20 h; consultant review within 24 h over 90%; care plan modification over 95%; just under half of seclusions monitored and documented per Trust guidelines.

audits.other_findings: Assault on staff was the indication in 80.4%; rapid tranquillisation in 45.7% and restraint in 84.8% of incidents; over half had psychotic symptoms.
audits.citation: Takao Y, Davis F, Saeger I, Ulhaq S, Refaat R. Re-audit of use of seclusion in a tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S108-S108. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.319.

audits.title: QI project: Improvement in quality of Seclusion Medical Review
audits.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice, NICE standards and Trust seclusion policy (time of review, reason, diagnosis, MSE, physical health and observations, medication and side effects, risk, plan)

cycle1.result: Above 90% for time of review, record keeping, management plan, risk, MSE and physical health; prescribed medications 60%, medication side effects 40%, physical observations 40%.

audits.intervention: Seclusion medical review template designed and incorporated into the existing documentation template, with teaching and training of doctors.

cycle2.result: Quality of seclusion medical review between 95% and 100%; no major concerns identified.

audits.other_findings: The project prompted nurses to audit nursing seclusion reviews.
audits.citation: Shahbaz S, Ward R. QI project: Improvement in quality of Seclusion Medical Review. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S218-S219. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.584.

audits.setting: Inpatient services, Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Above 80%: timing of review, record keeping, plan for continuing seclusion, risk to self and others, mental state examination. Below 60%: prescribed medications, medication side effects and physical observations.

audits.title: Audit Cycle on Medical Reviews of Seclusion in Medium and Low Secure Learning Disability Units
audits.standard: Trust policy SD28 'The use of seclusion and long-term segregation' and Mental Health Act Code of Practice 2015 chapter 26
audits.setting: Medium and low secure learning disability wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Initial medical review within first hour 34%; on-call consultant informed 50%; 4-hourly reviews 50%; responsible clinician present 67%; risk assessment 48%; medications commented on 20%.

audits.intervention: Education of colleagues working in secure services.

cycle2.period: One month, three months after actions
cycle2.result: Initial medical review within first hour 66%; on-call consultant informed 60%; 4-hourly reviews 66%; responsible clinician present 100%; risk assessment 89%; medications commented on 72%.

audits.other_findings: Physical health reviewed in 100% in both cycles; 34% of MDT reviews still had only 2 MDT members; comment on reducing restriction rose from 59% to 84%.
audits.citation: Iyer S, Williamson A. Audit Cycle on Medical Reviews of Seclusion in Medium and Low Secure Learning Disability Units. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S153-S153. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.435.

audits.title: Audit of Seclusion Practice in an Inpatient Adult Intellectual Disability (ID) Psychiatry Unit
audits.standard: NHS Highland Seclusion Policy: 15-minute monitoring, reviews at 2 and 4 hours, Datix on commencement
audits.setting: Inpatient adult intellectual disability assessment and treatment unit, NHS Highland

cycle1.result: Anxiolytic use before seclusion, respiration rate and appearance at 15-minute checks, plans to end seclusion at 2 hours and informing duty consultant at 4 hours often missing; Datix not always submitted. No figures reported.

audits.intervention: Results shared via Seclusion Policy Short Life Working Group, internal teaching, clinical governance forum and trainee induction; protocol drafts updated
audits.other_findings: Commonest reason for seclusion was increasing agitation and aggression. Re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Kumar P, Graves C, Jones S. Audit of Seclusion Practice in an Inpatient Adult Intellectual Disability (ID) Psychiatry Unit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S99-S99. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.295.

audits.title: Seclusion Pathway Review Audit
audits.standard: Trust seclusion policy: reviews and documentation of commencement, periodic reviews and termination (target 100%)
audits.setting: One adult male psychiatric intensive care unit and one adult female mental health ward

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 100%; initial medical review within 1 hour 81.82% (27); 2-hourly nursing review 93.94% (31); 4-hourly medical review on time 24/33; 8-hour MDT consultant review 78.79% (26); physical health observations 100%.

audits.other_findings: Delays in MDT review mainly when seclusion started at weekends or after hours. Recommendations: teaching, adding guidance to junior doctor handbook and induction, posters, and re-audit.
audits.citation: Alkasser M, Riadh M, Elsankary M, Merteen M. Seclusion Pathway Review Audit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S149-S149. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.402.

audits.title: An Audit of Clinicians Completing Independent Seclusion Reviews (Trust-Wide Audit Within Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear, NHS Foundation Trust)
audits.standard: CNTW seclusion policy: independent seclusion review must include an Approved Clinician
audits.setting: Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust (trust-wide)

cycle1.result: Senior clinicians at ISR: 83% medical, 11% non-medical AC, 6% neither; 68% of medical clinicians not AC grade; 0% of non-AC medical ISRs documented discussion with an AC; 29% out of hours.

audits.intervention: Seclusion policy changed so ISRs must be done by an AC except in extreme circumstances, when discussed with an AC
audits.other_findings: 96 of 260 seclusion episodes triggered an ISR; 72% of non-AC doctors were SHO grade.

audits.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice: medical review within 1 hour, 4-hourly until MDT review, twice daily thereafter, with specified content
audits.setting: Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 20% seen face-to-face within 1 hour; 75% seen 4-hourly until MDT review; mental health documented 97%, physical health 61%, medication 69%, rationale for continuing seclusion 72%; adverse medication effects and observation level 2%, risk to self 7%.

audits.other_findings: 5 seclusion episodes in 4 patients; a previous audit had not led to change.

audits.title: Audit of Seclusion: Evaluating Performance Against National and Local Standards
audits.standard: Trust Seclusion Policy and Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice
audits.setting: North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Incident forms completed in 83%, de-escalation attempted in 87%; NEWS incomplete in 82% at initiation. Doctor notified in all but one case (67% within 30 minutes); 100% had medical review, 39% within one hour and 29% after 120 minutes. Internal and external MDTs in 63% and 72%; 11% had neither. Termination reasons reported in 91%.

audits.intervention: None reported yet; recommendations in progress include staff training, policy updates, automated reminders, enhanced documentation, non-touch NEWS and virtual MDT meetings, to be monitored at re-audit.
audits.other_findings: Timing of Site Manager notification unclear in 93.5%. Night-time reviews suspended in 14 cases, 10 because the patient was asleep.
audits.citation: Javaid S, Mittal R, Jabbar Q, Bentley C, Dawson S. Audit of Seclusion: Evaluating Performance Against National and Local Standards. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S246-S247. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10611.

audits.title: Improving the Quality of SHO Seclusion Review Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Mental Health Units (Use of Force) Act 2018; target 80% compliance with all domains
audits.setting: South West London & St George's Mental Health NHS Trust; initial seclusion reviews by resident doctors

cycle1.result: 75% of reviews met all required criteria.

audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: seclusion proforma made accessible at handover, proforma circulated by email, teaching in the academic programme, and small-group core trainee teaching.

cycle2.result: 83% of reviews met all required criteria; minimal change in overall compliance on SPC chart.

audits.other_findings: Small numbers and variation between on-call doctors caused wide fluctuations. Risk assessment and physical health documentation improved; authors suggest mandatory completion of all domains.
audits.citation: Wilcha R, Viegas M, Morris L, McCloy-Smith E, Bell D. Improving the Quality of SHO Seclusion Review Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S215-S215. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11515.

audits.title: An Audit on Medical Seclusion Reviews in a Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit
audits.standard: SWYT seclusion and long-term segregation policy and seclusion toolkit (medical review within 1 hour, 4-hourly reviews, first MDT, independent MDT within 8-18 hours, daily reviews)
audits.setting: Psychiatric intensive care unit, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: First MDT within 08:00–22:00 next day 92.7%; out-of-hours reviews adherent 95%; daily non-RC medical reviews 87.2%; independent MDT reviews 24.2%; resident doctor review within 1 hour 64.4%; daily MDT reviews 66.6%.

audits.intervention: Recommended prompts for independent MDT reviews, seclusion toolkit in new doctors' induction and discussion with RCs on documentation.
audits.other_findings: Low daily MDT review figure was linked to incorrect documentation on the seclusion proforma.

audits.title: Improving Patient Safety in Inpatient Psychiatry: A Closed-Loop Audit of Seclusion Review Quality
audits.standard: Trust seclusion policy: eight core medical review criteria plus two best-practice criteria
audits.setting: Meadowbrook Unit inpatient mental health unit, Salford, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: No reviews met all eight criteria; most common number met was one (n=9). Physical health 70%, psychiatric health 40%, medication side effects 0%, harms of seclusion 2%, decision to continue 97%, steps to end seclusion 25%.

audits.intervention: Local teaching and presentations, communication to line managers and posters of trust standards in clinical areas.

cycle2.result: Seven reviews met all eight criteria; most common number met was four or five (n=12). Physical health 82%, psychiatric health 66%, medication side effects 19%, harms of seclusion 14%, decision to continue 91%, steps to end seclusion 23%.

audits.other_findings: Small declines in documenting the decision to continue and steps to end seclusion; asleep, senior-led and undocumented reviews may have affected 2025 results.
audits.citation: Do J, Runswick E, Malik S. Improving Patient Safety in Inpatient Psychiatry: A Closed-Loop Audit of Seclusion Review Quality. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S288-S288. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11731.
